Bioequivalence: 2x2 crossover analysis

Source: R/be_2x2.r
ks_be_2x2.Rd

Fits the standard two-period, two-sequence crossover model `response ~ sequence + treatment + period` (subject nested in sequence in the random term, `random = ~ seq | subject`) and returns the test-minus-reference treatment difference with its confidence interval. The sequence main effect absorbs carryover. This is the R twin of the SAS `PROC MIXED` bioequivalence analysis in the R tricks article (verified: estimate 0.0145, SE 0.0142, df 7, matching SAS `CL=DF=7`).

Usage

ks_be_2x2(
  data,
  response,
  trt,
  test,
  reference,
  seq,
  period,
  subject,
  log = TRUE,
  conf.level = 0.9
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per subject-period.

response

Unquoted name of the numeric response column.

trt

Unquoted name of the treatment column (factor with exactly the two levels named in `test` and `reference`).

test, reference

Character labels of the test and reference treatment levels (e.g. `"T"`, `"R"`).

seq, period, subject

Unquoted names of sequence, period, and subject columns.

log

Apply `log()` to the response before fitting (default `TRUE`, standard for BE on concentration data). Requires all responses positive.

conf.level

Confidence level; BE conventionally uses `0.90`.

Value

A list with `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `t`, `p.value`, `lcl`, `ucl` (log scale when `log = TRUE`), plus `ratio`, `ratio.lcl`, `ratio.ucl` on the original scale when `log = TRUE`.

Examples

cross <- data.frame(
  per = as.factor(rep(c(1, 2), 9)),
  trt = as.factor(c(rep(c("T", "R"), 4), rep(c("R", "T"), 5))),
  seq = as.factor(c(rep(1, 8), rep(2, 10))),
  cow = as.factor(rep(1:9, each = 2)),
  my  = c(29.9, 27.8, 54.0, 49.7, 41.6, 38.4, 28.5, 26.5, 22.2,
          21.4, 55.5, 49.1, 43.5, 41.3, 33.2, 34.3, 18.2, 17.1))
fit <- ks_be_2x2(cross, response = my, trt = trt, test = "T",
                 reference = "R", seq = seq, period = per, subject = cow)
c(TvR_log = fit$estimate, ratio = fit$ratio,
  lcl = fit$ratio.lcl, ucl = fit$ratio.ucl)
#>    TvR_log      ratio        lcl        ucl 
#> 0.01448831 1.01459377 0.98773441 1.04218353
